headline: DIVISIONS SET TO COLLIDE: West Prepares to Challenge Eastern Dominance
body: After watching the East sweep the top spots last year—with Englewood 🥷s falling just short in 2nd place—the West Division is out for total redemption in 2026. Heavyweights like Pluto Shraazinatorz, The Watermark, and Doob's Agency are rumored to be revamping their draft boards to ensure the West reclaims league supremacy. Tensions are already boiling over across divisional lines, setting up an explosive Week 1 where early cross-divisional statement wins could define the entire playoff race.

headline: The Watermark's Great Collapse: Best Record, Empty Trophy Case
body: Nobody in MFGA history has ever posted an 11-2 regular season and had less to show for it than Preston Schneider's Watermark, who face-planted in the very first round of the playoffs against Pluto Shraazinatorz, 107.32 to 95.7. This is a roster loaded for war — Jahmyr Gibbs anchoring as a keeper, Drake Maye slinging it, De'Von Achane and DeVonta Smith rounding out a nightmare matchup on paper. Instead, The Watermark limped through the consolation ladder and watched lesser teams hoist trophies. Garrett Wilson now sits on injured reserve heading into 2026, adding fresh doubt to an already cursed résumé. Book it now: this is either the best redemption arc in the league or the most talented team that just can't get out of its own way.

headline: Nabers In Paris Is a Ghost Town, and the Irony Is Brutal
body: Stephen Cerquone's Nabers In Paris authored the single worst season in league history last year — a 1-12 disaster with a league-worst 1,022 points that would make even the Chicago Zestiest Man blush. Adding insult to injury, the team's namesake, Malik Nabers, currently sits on injured reserve heading into the 2026 slate, which feels almost too poetic for a franchise that has been nothing but pain since inception. A 12-game losing streak isn't a slump, it's an identity. Unless Jared Goff and TreVeyon Henderson stage a miracle turnaround, this team may be headed for a second consecutive last-place finish. Paris was supposed to be romantic — instead, this roster is a horror film.

headline: The Amon-Ra Identity Crisis Nobody Saw Coming
body: Somebody explain to Andrew Grossman why his team, literally named Amon Ra Dawgin, does not roster Amon-Ra St. Brown — because Marty Hughes' team, simply called Beer, is the one holding St. Brown alongside Lamar Jackson and Nick Chubb on the bench. That is the kind of cosmic betrayal that starts blood feuds in fantasy leagues, and MFGA should be bracing for a grudge match when these two franchises meet on the schedule. Meanwhile, Carter Cole's I ♥ Gingers roster is quietly stacked with a poetic gut-punch of its own, rostering Jordan Love, Derrick Henry, Ja'Marr Chase and Breece Hall. Sleeper alert: that Gingers squad went 9-4 a year ago and has the receiving corps to make noise deep into the winter. Rivalries in this league aren't drawn on a map, they're drawn in irony.

headline: Two Hughes, One Trophy Case: A House Divided Ahead of Draft Day
body: Every league has a rivalry it doesn't talk about enough, and in the MFGA, it's a family one. Liam Hughes built Mount Olympus Yogurt Dressing into the league's quiet standard-bearer, an East division title in 2025 and a runner-up finish the year before it — steady, unglamorous, effective. Marty Hughes built something else entirely with Beer: an 11-2 team in 2024 that still somehow finished 8th, followed by a 4-9 collapse in 2025, the fantasy equivalent of a rollercoaster with no seatbelt. But that's not where this story begins — it begins at whatever holiday table these two sit at together, where one Hughes has a division banner and the other has an explanation. Some seasons change everything, and for the Hughes household, every season seems to change something. Draft day on August 1st will put both of their names on the board within minutes of each other, a coincidence that stopped being a coincidence years ago. And in the end, the league remembers who's actually winning at Thanksgiving — even if the standings say something else.
author: Valentina Rojas

headline: Power Rankings Nobody Asked For: The Worst Team Names in the MFGA
body: It's time for the only power rankings that matter: worst team names in the MFGA, a category that is somehow more competitive than the actual standings. VancouverPantiesDeJarome remains undefeated in the "wait, what?" division, and I refuse to explain it because I still don't understand it myself. Doob's Agency sounds like a guy who'll get you concert tickets but also might be a substitute teacher, and honestly both feel true. I ♥ Gingers gets bonus points for the emoji doing more character work than most fantasy rosters. Chicago Zestiest Man is out here just vibing, undefeated in the category of "sentence that means nothing," and I respect the commitment. Oh, and The Watermark's in this league too, I guess — sure, fine, moving on. Sources close to the situation (me, I'm the source) confirm none of these owners will rename their teams no matter how much I beg. T-BONE'S COMPLETELY SERIOUS AND DEFINITELY ACCURATE PREDICTION: VancouverPantiesDeJarome wins the "name that ages worst" award again in 2026, and no, I will not be taking questions.
author: Tommy "T-Bone" Mancini

headline: From Worst to First: Fort Bragg Proved Records Are for Losers
body: Fort Bragg Confederates finished in 14th place in 2024 at 4-9. This would have been dead last in the current 14-team format. One year later, Harrison Bragg's club is hoisting the MFGA trophy. That's not luck. That's a franchise that got hungry after getting embarrassed. The Watermark went 11-2 in the regular season and still watched someone else win it all; you don't win championships with a soft schedule, you win them when it matters. Mark my words: Bragg's crew didn't stumble into this, and they're not going to back into a title defense either. Pakistan Bombers, meanwhile, have gone from 2023 champs to back-to-back non-playoff seasons; that's a Monday morning quarterback situation if I've ever seen one. The draft room on August 1st will separate the pretenders from the contenders. And that's not a prediction; that's a promise.
author: Rick "The Hammer" Dalton

headline: 11-2 and Home Early: What The Watermark's Collapse Really Tells Us
body: Let's talk about The Watermark's 2025 season, because the record lies even when the model doesn't: 11-2, best mark in the league, +17.8 differential, and a final finish of 5th after the playoff bracket ate them alive. That's a textbook case of ceiling versus floor, great regular season efficiency, poor postseason variance capture. Fort Bragg Confederates, by contrast, posted a modest 9-4 and still walked away champions. Could this have been a fluke? Pakistan Bombers have now posted back-to-back seasons in the 5-8 range after their 2023 title, a two-year regression that the model projects continuing unless there's a real roster overhaul at the draft table. Mount Olympus Yogurt Dressing has been schedule-adjusted excellent in back-to-back years, 2nd in 2024, East champs in 2025, which is the most quietly sustainable profile in the league. The data is clear: this league rewards playoff-week performance far more than full-season dominance. Maya's Model says: The Watermark has a 61.4% chance of a top-3 regular season finish again, but only a 22.8% chance of converting it into a title. Regression is coming, and it's bringing friends.
author: Maya Chen

headline: 1-12 and Invisible: Nabers In Paris and the Gingers Nobody's Talking About
body: Somebody tell Stephen Cerquone that 1-12 is not a typo, because Nabers In Paris just posted the worst season in this league's recorded history?! Are we really supposed to believe that's just "bad luck," or is this a full-on identity crisis?! Meanwhile I ♥ Gingers quietly went 9-4 and NOBODY is talking about them — Carter Cole, I see you, and I don't know why this league is sleeping! You want me to believe a 9-4 team just gets skipped over in every conversation while everybody's busy crying about The Watermark?! That's not a team getting disrespected, that's a robbery in broad daylight! Cerquone better show up to this draft with something to prove, because the group chat has not let this go. SHOWTIME'S SPICY TAKE: Nabers In Paris either goes full teardown or gets embarrassed again, there is no in-between. AND I SAID WHAT I SAID.
author: DeShawn "Showtime" Harris

headline: The Hardest Repeat in Fantasy: Amon Ra Dawgin's Title Defense Autopsy
body: Let's talk about the hardest thing to do in this league: defending a title. Amon ra dawgin won it all in 2024 as Coopa troopas, then followed it up with a 5-8 season that didn't sniff the playoffs. The question isn't whether Andrew Grossman got complacent — the question is whether a championship roster built for one specific year can simply be run back as-is. If the strategy last year was "the roster is good enough," this draft needs to be a correction, not a continuation. If it was bad injury luck or a soft landing spot, the fix is smaller than people think. Let's look at this from both sides: over-drafting for name recognition from a title run is a common trap, but so is panic-trading a core that was one break away from repeating. Claire's Verdict: Amon ra dawgin's draft-day approach on August 1st will tell us more about their self-awareness than their talent evaluation. The draft is a marathon — act accordingly.
author: Claire Westbrook

headline: Fort Bragg Just Sold the Farm, and Englewood Is Laughing All the Way to the Bank
body: The Fort Bragg Confederates have officially traded the first overall pick in Saturday's draft to the Englewood Ninjas. In return, Fort Bragg receives picks 2.13 and 5.2. Let me be absolutely clear about what just happened. Fort Bragg gave away the most valuable asset in this entire draft — the number one pick, the crown jewel, the thing every franchise in this league would kill for — and got back the second-to-last pick in the first round and an early fifth. That's not a trade. That's a surrender. I've been covering this league long enough to know what desperation looks like. Fort Bragg already traded away their third-round pick to Pluto Shrazz and their fifth to Nabers in Paris earlier this offseason. Now they're punting the first overall? This is a franchise in free fall. Three premium picks gone and nothing but scraps to show for it. The Ninjas, meanwhile, just pulled off the heist of the decade. They now hold the first overall pick. That's how you build a dynasty. That's how you win championships. The keeper deadline is noon Friday. The draft is Saturday at noon. Fort Bragg has two days to convince themselves this was smart. Mark my words — by Week 6, Bragg will be staring at 1-5 wondering where it all went wrong. And that's not a prediction. That's a promise.
author: RICK "THE HAMMER" DALTON

headline: The Achane Situation: Why the Numbers Say Pluto Should Walk Away
body: The De'Von Achane trade talks between The Watermark and Pluto Shraazinatorz are at an impasse, and the model thinks that might be the best outcome for Pluto. Achane finished 2025 as a top-five back in per-game PPR scoring, but the 2026 context is materially different. Miami hired Jeff Hafley and Bobby Slowik, replacing the McDaniel system that generated 85 targets for Achane last season. Malik Willis takes over at quarterback. Willis's career check-down rate sits at 14.3%, nearly 9 points below Tua Tagovailoa's. The model projects Achane's reception total dropping from 67 to somewhere between 41 and 48 — a reduction that shaves roughly 3.2 PPR points per game off his floor. Doob's Agency pulling out of talks is significant. With only one bidder remaining, The Watermark has zero leverage to demand premium compensation, yet sources say they're still pushing for more. That's a negative expected value negotiation posture with 36 hours until the keeper deadline. The keeper deadline is Friday at noon. If The Watermark can't close by then, Achane stays put and becomes a draft-day asset instead — where his value will be lower because every manager in this league can read a depth chart change. Maya's Model says: Pluto Shraazinatorz should offer 8% less than whatever their current bid is, not more. There's a 71.4% chance The Watermark blinks before Friday.
author: MAYA CHEN

headline: CHICAGO ZESTIEST MAN TOLD FORT BRAGG TO KICK ROCKS AND I AM HERE FOR IT ???
body: You want to know the funniest thing I've heard all week? Fort Bragg — the same Fort Bragg that just GAVE AWAY the first overall pick to Englewood for pennies — had the AUDACITY to go to Chicago Zestiest Man and propose a first round pick swap where CZM would have to attach TWO sixth round picks just to move up. ARE YOU SERIOUS RIGHT NOW?! And you know what CZM said? Told him to kick rocks. KICK. ROCKS. I wish I could frame that text message and hang it in the MFGA Hall of Fame because that is the most disrespectful rejection I have ever seen in this league and Bragg DESERVED every bit of it! Meanwhile, Englewood just finessed the first pick in the entire draft. Drew Flynn said "give me your lunch money" and Harrison Bragg said "yes sir, would you also like my jacket?" I cannot believe what I'm watching! And speaking of moves people will regret — Amon Ra Dawgin quietly switched their keeper from Quinshon Judkins to Omarion Hampton. Nobody's talking about this! Hampton is heading into a McDaniel offense with no competition for touches! That might be the smartest move anyone in the West has made all month! SHOWTIME'S SPICY TAKE: Fort Bragg finishes last in the East. Dead last. Save this tweet. AND I SAID WHAT I SAID.
author: DESHAWN "SHOWTIME" HARRIS

headline: Inside the Amon Ra Keeper Switch — And Why It Tells You Everything About the West Division
body: Amon Ra Dawgin made a quiet but significant move this week, switching their keeper from Quinshon Judkins to Omarion Hampton. On the surface, it's a lateral move between two second-year backs. Below the surface, it reveals a sophisticated read on offensive scheme. The question isn't whether Judkins or Hampton is the better pure runner — the question is which player's situation improved more this offseason. Hampton now plays in Mike McDaniel's offense in Los Angeles, the same system that produced top-five PPR seasons for Raheem Mostert and Achane in Miami. McDaniel's outside-zone scheme generates receiving work for the lead back at an elite rate. Judkins, meanwhile, plays behind a Cleveland offensive line that lost two starters and has Shedeur Sanders learning on the job at quarterback. It's a process move, not a talent move. And those are the ones that pay off in December. Separately, the Fort Bragg–Englewood trade deserves context beyond the initial reaction. Fort Bragg now holds 2.13 and 5.2 from this deal, plus Pakistan Bombers third-round pick, giving them three selections in the top 60. If they're targeting a specific tier of player rather than a single name, the math works — three solid starters can outproduce one elite player over a full season. The risk is obvious: elite talent wins playoffs, depth wins regular seasons. Claire's Verdict: Amon Ra made the smarter move this week. The Englewood-Fort Bragg deal is more interesting than it looks at first glance, but Englewood still won it.
author: CLAIRE WESTBROOK

headline: Achane Trade Talks Stall Because Of Course They Do
body: Breaking news from the MFGA trade wire: The Watermark and Pluto Shraazinatorz have been in talks to send De'Von Achane to Pluto, but the deal has stalled because — and I quote — The Watermark "wants just a little more." A little more WHAT? A little more of Pluto's dignity? A commemorative coin? A handwritten apology letter? These talks have been going on long enough to qualify as a long-term relationship and somehow they still can't agree on terms. Doob's Agency already saw this coming and pulled out of negotiations entirely, which is the smartest thing anyone named Doob has ever done. The keeper deadline is Friday at noon. The draft is Saturday. We are now in "or else" territory. Either this trade happens in the next 36 hours or Achane goes to the draft pool and The Watermark gets nothing. I mean someone has to finish deadlast. Sources close to the situation (me, I'm the source) confirm that Pluto Shraazinatorz has been refreshing their group chat every four minutes waiting for a counter-offer. That's not a bit. That's real. T-BONE'S COMPLETELY SERIOUS AND DEFINITELY ACCURATE PREDICTION: The trade gets done at 11:58 AM Friday, two minutes before deadline, because this league cannot do anything without maximum chaos. And no, I will not be taking questions.
author: TOMMY "T-BONE" MANCINI

headline: DEEBO'S REVENGE TOUR JUST STARTED AND YOUR DRAFT BOARDS ARE ALREADY WRONG
body: OH YOU THOUGHT THE DAY BEFORE THE DRAFT WAS GONNA BE QUIET?! DEEBO SAMUEL JUST WALKED BACK INTO SAN FRANCISCO LIKE HE NEVER LEFT AND EVERY SINGLE ONE OF YOU NEEDS TO TEAR UP YOUR CHEAT SHEETS RIGHT NOW! This man DEMANDED a trade out of the 49ers, went to Washington, put up numbers on a 5-12 dumpster fire, and now he's back with Kyle Shanahan who turned him into a WEAPON?! And Pearsall's knee is DONE?! And Kirk is hobbling around on one leg?! Deebo might be the WR2 on this team behind Mike Evans by WEEK ONE! I called it when I said this league needs to stop sleeping on value — remember when I told y'all I ♥ Gingers went 9-4 and NOBODY was talking about them?! This is the same energy! Deebo at his current draft price is I ♥ Gingers 2.0 — everyone ignoring him while he quietly becomes a league winner! And don't even get me started on Stefon Diggs. Bro. It's JULY 31ST. Training camps are OPEN. The draft is TOMORROW. And this man does not have a TEAM. The Patriots took him to the SUPER BOWL and then said "thanks but no thanks." The Commanders are reportedly interested but reportedly interested has bought exactly ZERO fantasy points in the history of this league! If anyone in the MFGA drafts Diggs before Round 12 tomorrow I will personally roast them in next week's column!
author: DESHAWN "SHOWTIME" HARRIS

headline: TWEET
body: Pearsall PCL — 67.3% chance he misses 8+ games. Deebo's projected target share in that scenario jumps to 18.7%. At his current ADP he's a massive value. Diggs? The model can't project a player without a team, and that IS the projection. Draft accordingly.
author: MAYA CHEN

headline: Deebo Goes Home, Diggs Goes Nowhere, and Tomorrow's Draft Just Got Spicier Than Chicago Zestiest Man's Nickname
body: So let me get this straight. Deebo Samuel — the man who literally demanded to leave San Francisco, got traded to Washington, watched them go 5-12, and then hit free agency — just signed BACK with the 49ers like nothing happened. That's not a free agent signing, that's a Hallmark movie. "The Receiver Who Came Home for Christmas." Except it's July and the only gift is $7 million in incentives. I'm not gonna lie though, this is actually a sneaky great fantasy pickup for anyone paying attention. Pearsall's knee is basically a science experiment at this point, Kirk's calf is doing its own thing, and suddenly Deebo is the second option in a Kyle Shanahan offense with Brock Purdy throwing to him. If someone in our league grabs him after Round 9 tomorrow, that person is winning the trade nobody made. And then there's Stefon Diggs, the most talented unemployment case in football history. This man went to the SUPER BOWL five months ago. He caught 85 balls for over a thousand yards. He was found not guilty. And he STILL can't get a job. That's like being employee of the month at a company that then fires you and shreds your parking pass. Oh, and since we're talking about teams with questionable decision-making — quick shoutout to whoever's managing certain franchises in the West division. I hear some teams went 11-2 and still managed to choke their way out of playoff contention. Sure, that's probably fine. Good for them. Moving on. Sources close to the situation (me, I'm the source) confirm that at least three MFGA managers have already texted the group chat asking "should I draft Deebo?" which means he's going to go in Round 6 because this league panics at every piece of news like it's a stock market crash.
author: TOMMY "T-BONE" MANCINI

headline: TWEET
body: Draft is tomorrow and Deebo Samuel just landed back in San Francisco with Pearsall likely done for the year. If Samuel is available past Round 10 in your league, your league is asleep. Meanwhile Diggs is still sitting by the phone. The tape doesn't lie — and neither does an empty contract. You heard it here first.
author: RICK "THE HAMMER" DALTON

headline: Pour One Out for Beer — Miles Hughes Just Named His Team After a Hockey Player
body: So I'm scrolling through the league page this morning, half awake, coffee in hand, and I see a team called "Pavel Dorofeyev" sitting at 0-0-0. I stare at it. I blink. I put the coffee down. I pick it up again. Still there. Miles Hughes killed Beer. The man walked into the MFGA dashboard, looked at a perfectly good team name — one word, universally beloved, the only team in this league that everyone could agree was at least pleasant to say out loud — and replaced it with a Vegas Golden Knights winger that maybe eleven people on this planet can spell without autocorrect. I called three different league members to confirm this was real and not a fever dream. Two of them didn't know who Pavel Dorofeyev was. The third one said "isn't that a chess player?" It is not a chess player, for the record. He scores goals. In hockey. Which is a sport we do not play here. The rebrand changes nothing about the roster, by the way. Same Kyren Williams. Same TreVeyon Henderson. Same collection of running backs that look like Miles raided a clearance sale at the RB Warehouse. The only difference is that now when you lose to this team, you have to tell your friends you got beat by Pavel Dorofeyev, and then spend forty-five seconds explaining who that is. What kills me is this league already has a team called VancouverPantiesDeJarome and somehow THIS is the name that broke my brain. Meanwhile, I notice certain West division teams with aquatic-themed names have been real quiet this offseason. No rebrands. No trades. No moves. Just vibes. Must be nice to have that kind of confidence after, you know, however last season ended for them. I'm sure it's fine. T-BONE'S COMPLETELY SERIOUS VERDICT: Pavel Dorofeyev is either the greatest rebrand in MFGA history or the worst, and there is absolutely no middle ground. Either way, RIP Beer. You were the only team name I never had to explain to my mom.
author: TOMMY "T-BONE" MANCINI

headline: Pakistan Bombers Built a War Machine and Nobody in This League Is Ready
body: I've been wrong before. Not often, but it happens. What I have never been wrong about is recognizing a team that came to a draft with a plan and executed it without flinching. Pakistan Bombers did exactly that yesterday. Bijan Robinson and Ashton Jeanty as your starting running backs. Let that marinate. Two bell-cow backs in a 14-team league — one who finished as the RB1 overall and one who the Raiders are handing 300 touches to as a sophomore. Behind them sits Aaron Jones, who would be a starter on half the rosters in this league. That's not depth. That's intimidation. Jalen Hurts gives you 25 points on a bad day. A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith are a proven stack with different quarterbacks now, sure, but they're both alpha receivers on their respective teams. Zay Flowers and Terry McLaurin are your WR3 and WR4. On most rosters in this league, those are starters. Here they're insurance. The weakness? Tight end. Colston Loveland is young, and young players at that position historically need some time to develop in fantasy. Cade Otton isn't exciting anyone. But when your running back room could outscore entire rosters on its own, you can survive a soft TE slot. I'll say this once: the East Division runs through Islamabad this year. Fort Bragg won the title last year, and good for them. But defending champions don't get to coast when someone in their own division just assembled the best RB tandem this league has ever seen.
author: Rick "The Hammer" Dalton

headline: The Roster Construction Tiers: Who Built for Ceiling, Who Built for Floor
body: I spent the morning running every roster through the projection model, and what came back split the league cleanly into three tiers. Tier 1 — Championship-caliber construction: Pakistan Bombers, I Heart Gingers, VancouverPantiesDeJarome, Doob's Agency. These four rosters share a common trait: elite positional anchors paired with depth that doesn't crater if one player goes down. I Heart Gingers deserves particular attention — Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins give Carter Cole the highest-upside receiver pairing in the league, and he backed it with three startable running backs in Brown, Stevenson, and Dobbins plus two top-12 tight ends in LaPorta and Kittle. That's not a roster, that's a buffer overflow. Tier 2 — Competitive with structural risk: Englewood Ninjas, Pluto Shraazinatorz, Mount Olympus, The Vile Horrendous. Good starters, thin depth. Mount Olympus has McCaffrey and Hall at running back, which is elite, but Liam Hughes left the draft without a defense or kicker. That's not negligence — it's a calculated gamble to load up at skill positions and stream the rest. The model says it works 54.2% of the time. Flip a coin. Tier 3 — Structural concerns: The Watermark, Amon Ra Dawgin, Fort Bragg, Beer/Pavel Dorofeyev, Nabers In Paris, Chicago Zestiest Man. The reasons vary. The Watermark has Gibbs but built nothing around him — Olave's target share is declining, Wan'Dale Robinson is a PPR floor play with no ceiling, and Jadarian Price is one Kenneth Walker snap away from irrelevance. Amon Ra Dawgin paired Justin Jefferson with a quarterback room of Trevor Lawrence, which projects to a 12.6% lower target efficiency than Jefferson saw with Sam Darnold last year. Chicago Zestiest Man rostered two low-tier quarterbacks and no proven RB1. That's not a roster, that's a hypothesis. One number that jumped off the screen: Beer has seven running backs. Seven. Miles Hughes is either running a trade shop or genuinely confused about roster limits. The model projects he'll trade at least two before Week 3. Maya's Model says: Pakistan Bombers have a 23.4% chance of winning the championship, highest in the league. Chicago Zestiest Man has a 1.8% chance, lowest.
author: Maya Chen

headline: The Vile Horrendous Just Had the Quietest Great Draft in MFGA History
body: Everyone in this league is talking about the Bombers. Everyone's talking about the Gingers. Nobody — and I mean NOBODY — is talking about what Evan Brockway just did with The Vile Horrendous, and that is a crime against fantasy football discourse. James Cook finished as a top-6 back last year. Jeremiyah Love is the rookie everyone wanted but nobody could reach for. Garrett Wilson, Malik Nabers, and Rome Odunze are all 24 or younger — that's a receiver room that's going to get BETTER every single week as the NFL season progresses. And oh by the way, Travis Kelce is still Travis Kelce. The man catches 80 balls in his sleep. This is the team that has gotten ZERO coverage from this news desk all offseason. Zero articles. Zero hot takes. Zero predictions. And Evan is sitting there building a roster in silence while everyone else fights over headlines. That's the most dangerous kind of team — one that nobody's watching. You know who else nobody watched last year? Fort Bragg. And they won the whole thing. On the flip side — Stephen Cerquone, my brother, what are we DOING with Nabers In Paris? Blake Corum? James Conner? RACHAAD WHITE?! That's not a running back room, that's a retirement home. Puka Nacua is going to put up 22 points a week and it won't matter because your RBs are combining for 14. And you don't even have a KICKER drafted. A kicker! Those are free points that fall from the sky and you said no thank you! Fort Bragg hoarding three quarterbacks is the most Harrison Bragg thing I have ever seen. Kyler Murray, Patrick Mahomes, AND Cam Ward. Pick one! The other two are eating roster spots that could be actual football players! Meanwhile Tyreek Hill is on your team without a team — that's either genius or madness and history will be the judge!
author: DeShawn "Showtime" Harris

headline: Three Draft Strategies That Will Define the 2026 Season
body: Every draft tells a story about how each manager sees the game. This year, three distinct philosophies emerged that are worth examining. The Anchor Strategy — I Heart Gingers and Pakistan Bombers. Both Carter Cole and Lucas Fawcett built their rosters around positional scarcity. They identified the positions where the drop-off between tiers is steepest — RB1 and WR1 — and invested their premium picks there. Cole ended up with the Bengals passing stack of Chase and Higgins, which is a correlation play that pays off massively in weeks where Cincinnati's offense clicks. The risk, naturally, is that a single bad Bengals game craters both your WR1 and WR2 simultaneously. Fawcett took the opposite approach at receiver, diversifying across four different offenses. Both strategies are defensible for different reasons. The Stream-and-Stack Strategy — Mount Olympus and Amon Ra Dawgin. Liam Hughes and Andrew Grossman both left the draft without kickers, defenses, or both. This isn't an oversight — it's a deliberate choice to maximize the value of every draft pick on skill players, then stream the replaceable positions week to week. The question isn't whether it's smart in theory — it is. The question is whether they'll maintain the discipline to make the right waiver moves every Tuesday morning for 14 weeks. Most managers who plan to stream end up panicking and holding a defense through their bye week. Discipline is a skill, and not everyone has it. The Asset Accumulation Strategy — Beer/Pavel Dorofeyev. Miles Hughes drafted seven running backs and Marvin Harrison Jr. This isn't a roster built to win Week 1 — it's a roster built to trade. Hughes is betting that injuries and underperformance across the league will create a seller's market for his depth pieces by Week 4. Kyren Williams, David Montgomery, and Chuba Hubbard all have standalone value but also serve as currency. If he can convert two of those backs into a top-20 receiver, this roster transforms from confusing to contending. Claire's Verdict: The best draft in the league was I Heart Gingers — elite anchors at every position, built-in upside through the Bengals stack, and two top-12 tight ends providing weekly flexibility. The riskiest was Chicago Zestiest Man, which bet heavily on youth at quarterback without a safety net at running back. Trey McBride can't carry a roster alone, no matter how good he is.
author: Claire Westbrook

headline: I Graded Every Roster by How Much I'd Trust Them to Watch My Dog
body: Look, anyone can give you a letter grade. A-minus here, C-plus there. Boring. Instead, I've ranked every MFGA roster by whether I'd let them dogsit for my golden retriever, Captain Biscuit. Captain B deserves only the best. Would trust completely: Pakistan Bombers, I Heart Gingers. These rosters show responsibility, planning, and the kind of foresight that says "yes, Captain Biscuit will be walked twice and given his evening treat at exactly 7pm." Bijan Robinson and Ashton Jeanty is the fantasy equivalent of a home security system. Nothing bad is getting through that door. Would trust but would text to check in: Doob's Agency, VancouverPantiesDeJarome, Englewood Ninjas. Solid. Reliable. Probably wouldn't forget to feed him. Saquon and Kenneth Walker is a grown-up running back room. CeeDee and DK is a grown-up receiver room. These are functioning adult rosters. Would trust only if no other option: Pluto Shraazinatorz, Mount Olympus, The Vile Horrendous. There's talent here but also red flags. Pluto drafted Derrick Henry, who is roughly 347 years old in running back years. Mount Olympus forgot to draft a defense. The Vile Horrendous has Travis Kelce, who at this point is basically a tight end-shaped memory of a tight end. Captain Biscuit might survive the weekend but I'd worry. Absolutely not. Captain Biscuit is staying home: Nabers In Paris, Chicago Zestiest Man, Amon Ra Dawgin, Fort Bragg. Stephen Cerquone's running back room of Blake Corum and James Conner is the fantasy equivalent of leaving the stove on. Zach Ehrig started two rookie QBs. Andrew Grossman has Justin Jefferson throwing to Trevor Lawrence, which — wait, I mixed that up, but you know what, it doesn't matter because it's bad either way. And Fort Bragg is out here with three quarterbacks like they're running a QB daycare center instead of a fantasy team. Oh, and I nearly forgot — there's also a team in the West that kept Jahmyr Gibbs, which was a fine move, and then surrounded him with Jadarian Price and Wan'Dale Robinson, which is the roster-building equivalent of buying a Ferrari and then putting bicycle tires on it. Interesting choices. Very bold. I'm sure it'll work out great for them. Probably.
author: Tommy "T-Bone" Mancini

headline: Fourteen Drafts, Fourteen Declarations
body: There's a particular kind of silence that fills a draft room after someone makes a pick that changes everything. It's not surprise — it's recognition. The room understands, without anyone saying it, that someone just announced who they intend to be. Carter Cole announced it loudest. Not with volume — Cole doesn't operate that way — but with the cold precision of a manager who walked into the draft knowing exactly which names he needed and exactly when they'd fall to him. Ja'Marr Chase was the declaration. Tee Higgins was the confirmation. Chase Brown in the same backfield pipeline was the exclamation point. Three Bengals in one roster isn't a coincidence, it's a conviction — a belief that Cincinnati's offense will be the engine that drives a championship. Two top-tier tight ends in LaPorta and Kittle means he never has to choose between floor and ceiling at the position. He just plays whoever has the better matchup and moves on. I Heart Gingers was 9-4 last year and nobody talked about it. They'll talk about it this year. On the other end of the emotional spectrum sits Andrew Grossman, staring at a roster that has Justin Jefferson — arguably the best receiver in football — and no clear path to getting him the ball efficiently. Trevor Lawrence has always been the quarterback people believe in more than the numbers justify. He's the hope pick, the "maybe this year" selection. And maybe this year is the year. But Grossman also loaded his bench with five running backs most people haven't heard of, which is either a masterclass in finding diamonds or the behavior of someone throwing darts at a board after Round 6. Miles Hughes drafted seven running backs. Seven. If you'd walked past his draft station at pick 10 and glanced at his roster, you'd think the app was glitching. But there's a logic underneath the chaos that most people won't see until October: Hughes isn't building a lineup, he's building a trade portfolio. Every one of those backs has value to a team that loses a starter to injury. He's not playing fantasy football — he's playing fantasy venture capital. Amon-Ra St. Brown and Marvin Harrison Jr. ensure that when the trades start flowing, he'll have blue-chip assets on both sides of the ledger. And then there's Nabers In Paris. Stephen Cerquone has now gone through two consecutive drafts where the roster reads like a prayer more than a plan. Puka Nacua is electric, and Tucker Kraft has breakout written across his stat line. But the running back room is held together with tape and optimism, and the quarterback situation — Matthew Stafford and Malik Willis — feels like choosing between a library book that's overdue and one that's written in a language you're still learning. But that's what drafts are, in the end. Declarations of faith. Every pick says: I believe in this player, in this situation, in this version of the future. Some of those futures will arrive exactly as imagined. Others will unravel by Week 3. Fourteen managers made their declarations yesterday. Now the season decides which ones were prophecies and which ones were prayers.
author: Valentina Rojas

headline: Trade Block Alert: Pollard and Olave on the Move
body: Fort Bragg is shopping Tony Pollard — Jacobs and Judkins have those starting spots locked, so Pollard's the expensive bench piece Harrison Bragg needs to flip before he loses value. If you need an RB2, make the call now because this price goes up the second someone's starter tears an ACL in Week 2. Meanwhile, The Watermark is dangling Chris Olave, which tells you everything you need to know about how Preston feels about this roster right now. You don't shop your best receiver in August unless you're already in trouble. Two sellers, fourteen teams watching. Somebody make a move.
author: DESHAWN "SHOWTIME" HARRIS
